Welcome to Steve Webster and congratulations to Duncan, David, Kevin, Dean, Gavin, Nadir and Saul on gaining representative honours. 14th OCTOBER 1984 COLLINGWOOD OPEN - 3 MILES
Young Kevin retained his title pretty comfortably from another second generation Belgravian, David Couzens, although Tom Carter did give him a bit of a fright in his semi-final.
Stage 2: Kevin Nash had run a stormer on leg 2 at Stockley Park eight days earlier and a similar effort with a sub-17 timing was hoped for here.

Most of our lads made more conservative starts but after the first of the 2 mile circuits we seemed to be leading from Brighton & Hove with Yitbarek 4th and Kevin Nash, Charles Herrington and Rob McHarg all in the first 15.

Lee Hurst was now our leading man in 44th, Paul Freary 52nd, Jason Lobo 60th Charles Herrington 70th, Kevin Nash 76th and Alaster Stewart 95th - a score of just under 400 and already a set of medals looked unlikely.
In muddy conditions Taylor, Belgrave's Kevin Nash and South London's Stuart Major broke away early with Staines of South London not far behind.

Among the next results, the discus found Kevin Brown in 2nd which was better than expected and Phillips Idowu was only 16 centimetres short of his best in winning the triple jump while the Frenchman fell short of his by some way; we were on song.

In the javelin Wesley was our 'A' man and showed a useful improvement to 54m+ while Kevin Brown filled the 'B' slot. Kevin had beaten Lee Newman in a close discus competition but Lee gained good points in the shot while new man Dave Readle celebrated his first outing for Belgrave by winning the 'B' shot.
Our condolences go to Bert's wife Margaret who shared his many interests, including membership of Belgrave Harriers, and to their sons Kevin, Mark and John.

Last year Kevin Nash had to pull out of the team with a knee problem. No such bad luck this time as Kevin confirmed his fine run in the Southern event and moved the Bels a couple of seconds closer to Birchfield.
